title: Others borrowing his solos: Goodman record, Johnny Long, Ella Fitzgerald
summary: He recalls his tag on It's Got to Be This or That, Johnny Long arranging his Shantytown solo without paying him, and Ella quoting his Lady Be Good solo as a compliment.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: That's for sure. And of course, there were a lot of recordings that I made which were not under my name, I didn't write the music to them or anything like that, but there were quite a few recordings that I've made, if I can remember, that -- special ones, I might say, that I recorded with Benny Goodman, you know, and Art Tatum, and sometimes a couple of recordings stick out in my mind, like one recording I made with Benny Goodman, the big band, Benny Goodman's big
band, back in the '40s. You may remember, it's called "It's Got To Be This or That."
Oh, yeah, you mentioned that earlier on the tape.
Yeah, that's right.
And you ended with saying --
Did I mention how I ended it?
I think so, but you can put it in again.
But anyway, 'It's got to be this or that,' and I say it in a deep voice, a false voice like, 'It's got to be this or that.'
(Laughter.)
I may have said that before.
Right, you did say it. But it bears repetition.
(Laughter.)
Now you also had some solos of yours and some of the improvisations were used by other people, weren't they?
Well, yes. I made a recording of 'In Old Shantytown.'
'It's only a shanty in old Shantytown.'

'Only a shanty in old Shantytown,' which along comes Johnny Long and his group, they took one of my solos and did every -- did a thing, arrangement, on every note that I played in one of my solos on recording.
Did you receive any royalties --
Never received a cent from that.
Did they acknowledge that it came from -- that you were the source of it?
Yeah.
They did acknowledge that though?
But what could I do?
Right. Now, who else?
Well, let's see. I can't remember at the moment.
Oh, Ella Fitzgerald.

Ella. Oh, well, anyway, in Ella's case, she took a few bars of another recording that I had made, 'Lady Be Good.' And she took a few bars and which was more a compliment to me. She took a few bars of one of my solos in 'Lady Be Good' and riffed it the same way that I played it, you know, and that was more or less a compliment, you know.
So she didn't take a whole chorus. She just took a --
No, not a whole chorus.
-- section, maybe like a half chorus or something.
Yeah. And at the end of that particular chorus that she took, she mentioned my name.
Uh-huh, this is Slam Stewart here, right.
That made that real nice. I enjoyed that.
That was a little bit more -- that was a little bit closer to a tribute than a pickpocket.
That's for sure, yes.
